output.name: Halkiri

anatomy.part: head and beak tip of the tern
breast, the bright heart of the body
right trailing feathers, where the wing returns to the body

output.myth: Ithúna sent her word across the sound on a tern, the way you send a tern when the boats are out and the wind is wrong. She sewed its wings herself from goat-gut cloth. Ennu the Kite-Wright gave her two bones for the frame and told her not to fly it in a Tavo wind. She flew it anyway. The Gale took the tern and turned it over the ice-grounds, and her husband heard the calling through the cold and turned his boat for home. The tern went back and forth across the sound all that winter, until the string wore thin in the middle. Some say it still goes that way in the north when the wind is right, carrying a message nobody can read now. The Gulls say the tern is still flying and the husband is still on his way. Hesk keeps count of the trips. She says there are more than anyone has counted.
output.verse:
Back across the sound,
the tern goes with the north wind,
still calling him home.
